database_summary: Traffic collisions dataset with three related tables: collisions (one row per collision/case_id, includes location, time, severity, counts), parties (one row per involved party/person/vehicle in a collision), and victims (one row per victim/involved person with injury and seating/safety info). case_ids is a small lookup linking case_id to db_year. The schema is event-oriented (collisions are events), parties and victims are event-related rows (participants, measurements). Joins from collisions -> parties or victims are one-to-many and can multiply rows; case_ids is a simple 1:1 (or 1:many by year) lookup.

accepted.name: collisions_core
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  case_id,
  jurisdiction,
  officer_id,
  reporting_district,
  chp_shift,
  population,
  county_city_location,
  county_location,
  beat_type,
  chp_beat_type,
  primary_road,
  secondary_road,
  distance,
  direction,
  weather_1,
  weather_2,
  road_surface,
  road_condition_1,
  lighting,
  control_device,
  collision_severity,
  killed_victims,
  injured_victims,
  party_count,
  primary_collision_factor,
  hit_and_run,
  type_of_collision,
  motor_vehicle_involved_with,
  tow_away,
  state_highway_indicator,
  state_route,
  postmile,
  location_type,
  latitude,
  longitude,
  collision_date,
  collision_time,
  process_date
FROM collisions
accepted.description: Canonical projection of collisions table exposing core event attributes and measures. Use this as the base cohort for filtering collisions by date, location, severity, or aggregated with parties/victims. | Use for: Filter collisions by date range, county, road or severity; Map collisions with latitude/longitude or cluster by postmile/state_route; Baseline cohort for joining parties or victims

Use this when analyzing participant-level attributes (age, sex, at_fault, safety equipment) or aggregating party-level measures per collision. | Use for: Aggregate participant injury/fault by age/sex/vehicle type; Identify at-fault drivers and their attributes; Join to collisions to analyze context around participant roles

accepted.name: victims_person_profile
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  case_id,
  party_number,
  victim_role,
  victim_sex,
  victim_age,
  victim_degree_of_injury,
  victim_seating_position,
  victim_safety_equipment_1,
  victim_safety_equipment_2,
  victim_ejected
FROM victims
accepted.description: Normalized projection of victims exposing injury degree, age, sex, seating and safety equipment. Use for victim-level injury analysis or to join against parties by case_id+party_number. | Use for: Count injured victims by injury severity, age group, or seating position; Join to parties by case_id+party_number to correlate party attributes with victim outcomes; Filter victims by ejection or safety equipment usage

accepted.name: collision_party_counts
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  case_id,
  COUNT(*) AS parties_total,
  SUM(CASE WHEN at_fault = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS parties_at_fault,
  SUM(CASE WHEN COALESCE(cellphone_in_use,0) != 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS parties_cellphone_in_use,
  SUM(COALESCE(party_number_killed,0)) AS parties_killed_count,
  SUM(COALESCE(party_number_injured,0)) AS parties_injured_count,
  AVG(party_age) AS avg_party_age
FROM parties
GROUP BY case_id
accepted.description: Per-collision aggregated counts of party-level indicators: total parties, number at fault, number with cellphone in use, number killed/injured. Useful to join back to collisions for event-level modeling or to filter high-risk collisions. | Use for: Find collisions with many parties or many at-fault parties; Enrich collision rows with party-derived measures before modeling; Filter collisions where cellphone use was prevalent among parties

accepted.name: collision_victim_counts
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  case_id,
  COUNT(*) AS victims_total,
  SUM(CASE WHEN victim_degree_of_injury = 'killed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS victims_killed_count,
  SUM(CASE WHEN victim_degree_of_injury = 'severe injury' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS victims_severe_injury_count,
  SUM(CASE WHEN victim_degree_of_injury = 'complaint of pain' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS victims_complaint_of_pain_count,
  SUM(CASE WHEN victim_ejected = 'ejected' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS victims_ejected_count,
  AVG(victim_age) AS avg_victim_age
FROM victims
GROUP BY case_id
accepted.description: Per-collision aggregated counts of victims by injury severity and safety flags. Use to measure collision-level victim outcomes and join with collisions for analysis. | Use for: Rank collisions by number of killed or severely injured victims; Compare victim outcomes across roads or counties; Create incident severity labels combining counts

accepted.name: parties_rank_within_collision
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  case_id,
  party_number,
  party_type,
  party_sex,
  party_age,
  at_fault,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY case_id ORDER BY CASE WHEN party_number IS NULL THEN 9999 ELSE party_number END, id) AS party_rank
FROM parties
accepted.description: Ranks parties within each collision by party_number (or insertion order). Exposes party_rank so callers can implement top-k party selection per collision deterministically. | Use for: Select the first N parties per collision for downstream analysis; Identify primary driver by lowest party_number when party_number encodes ordering

accepted.name: collisions_enriched
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  ca.case_id,
  ca.county_location,
  ca.primary_road,
  ca.collision_date,
  ca.collision_time,
  ca.collision_severity,
  ca.killed_victims,
  ca.injured_victims,
  COALESCE(pc.parties_total,0) AS parties_total,
  COALESCE(pc.parties_at_fault,0) AS parties_at_fault,
  COALESCE(vc.victims_total,0) AS victims_total,
  COALESCE(vc.victims_killed_count,0) AS victims_killed_count,
  COALESCE(vc.victims_severe_injury_count,0) AS victims_severe_injury_count,
  ca.latitude,
  ca.longitude
FROM collisions ca
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT case_id, COUNT(*) AS parties_total, SUM(CASE WHEN at_fault = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS parties_at_fault
  FROM parties
  GROUP BY case_id
) pc ON pc.case_id = ca.case_id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT case_id, COUNT(*) AS victims_total, SUM(CASE WHEN victim_degree_of_injury = 'killed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS victims_killed_count, SUM(CASE WHEN victim_degree_of_injury = 'severe injury' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS victims_severe_injury_count
  FROM victims
  GROUP BY case_id
) vc ON vc.case_id = ca.case_id
accepted.description: Collision-level denormalized view: collisions left-joined to aggregated party and victim summaries. Use this to run event-level analyses without repeatedly joining lower-level tables. | Use for: Event-level modeling combining collision attributes and aggregated participant outcomes; Map collisions with counts of parties and victims; Filter collisions by both location and aggregated participant outcomes
